terminal_record.title: Trump Issues NSPM-4 Expanding the Military Role on Southern Border Lands
terminal_record.description_short: Trump’s April 11, 2025 NSPM-4 directs a larger military role on federal border lands; CRS describes limited temporary detention authority there.
terminal_record.description_medium: On April 11, 2025, Trump issued National Security Presidential Memorandum 4 (NSPM-4), directing agencies to expand the military role on specified federal lands along the southern border, including the Roosevelt Reservation. A Congressional Research Service analysis says the military jurisdiction could permit temporary detention of migrants attempting to cross before transfer to law enforcement. The sources describe a border operation, not the general emergency detention power alleged in the frozen entry.
terminal_record.description_long:
On April 11, 2025, President Donald Trump issued National Security Presidential Memorandum 4, titled “Military Mission for Sealing the Southern Border of the United States and Repelling Invasions.” It directed the Secretaries of Defense, Interior, Agriculture, and Homeland Security to take actions for a larger military role on federal lands along the southern border, including the Roosevelt Reservation and excluding Federal Indian Reservations from the specified land provision. The memorandum also invoked emergency-related authority for certain public-land withdrawals.

A May 5 Congressional Research Service analysis said the military jurisdiction established for a border area could allow soldiers to control access and temporarily detain migrants and traffickers attempting to cross, before transferring them to appropriate law enforcement. CRS attributed that description to the Department of Defense. This is a geographically limited border operation, not the general authority to detain civilians during any emergency asserted in the frozen entry. The original April 1 date and executive-order label are incorrect: the sourced event is an April 11 presidential memorandum. The documents do not set out the claimed general martial-law framework or a bypass of civilian courts, and they do not establish that the policy resulted in unrelated civilian detentions.

source_fact_map.fact: The White House published NSPM-4 on April 11, 2025.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
# Military Mission for Sealing the Southern Border of the United States and Repelling Invasions

April 11, 2025

NATIONAL SECURITY PRESIDENTIAL MEMORANDUM/NSPM-4

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Section 1. Policy.
